question: A report by Frontex’s Fundamental Rights Office, which has been made public, reveals the prolonged inaction of the Greek Coast Guard in the Pylos shipwreck case, which cost the lives of more than 600 refugees and migrants on 14 June 20231. The report concludes that the ‘immediate focus prior to the shipwreck was not rescue’, and suggests the boat may have capsized as a result of the attempt to tow it.

It also highlights that: the Greek authorities did not start the search and rescue operation as soon as Frontex informed them about it but when the boat had already capsized; the attempts to assist the boat put passengers on board the Adriana in greater danger; the coast guard vessel recorded the dangerous rocking of the Adriana; connecting ropes to the migrant boat bore significant risks; and the resources deployed were insufficient.

These were precisely the conclusions drawn at two events I recently organised in Brussels and Athens to shed light on the causes and circumstances of the deadly shipwreck. At these events, we heard from experts, analysts and lawyers, and from survivors who revealed that the Coast Guard abandoned them when the migrant boat sunk.2 In view of this: 1.
Will the Commission seek explanations and an update from the Greek authorities?
How does it comment on the delay in the investigations of the judicial authorities and the risk of a cover-up?
answer: EN on behalf of the European Commission (7.5.2024) 1. The Commission takes the findings of the Serious Incident Report (SIR) by the Frontex Fundamental Rights Officer (FRO) very seriously.

The SIR focuses on actions taking place in the context of Frontex Joint Operations and does not absolve the national authorities from their obligation to investigate allegations of wrongdoing in the most transparent, thorough, and prompt way possible.

Should the outcome of the national investigations confirm the FRO’s findings, the Commission expects the Greek authorities to prosecute any identified wrongdoings fully, as this is within their responsibility. 2. The Commission is in regular contact with the Greek authorities and continues to call for the ongoing national investigations and judicial proceedings to be conducted in a swift and comprehensive manner.
The Commission will keep monitoring developments in this context closely.
